increments.title: Make Copy as new create both the notification and fulfilment aggregates
increments.diagnosis:
"Copy as new" produces a half-created notification in real mode (the mode the workspace stack runs — `docker/stack/frontend.compose.yml:52` sets `LIVE_ANIMALS_MODE=real`, and `frontend:src/server/app/services/mode.js:1` defaults to `real`).

The backend keeps two independent aggregates per reference number: `Notification` and `NotificationFulfilments`. `backend:src/main/java/.../notificationfulfilments/NotificationFulfilmentsService.java:24-31` shows the fulfilments service has no dependency on the notification side at all — nothing links them except the frontend writing to both.

Every other lifecycle operation in the frontend's real adapter dual-writes, and the code says so explicitly: `frontend:src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/transition.js:6-10` ("Every lifecycle transition dual-writes: one call to the canonical fulfilment endpoint, one to the notification endpoint"), and `frontend:.../real/lifecycle/create.js:7-10` documents the ordering rule ("Notification mints the reference number ... then the notification-fulfilments aggregate is bootstrapped at that same ref via PUT /notification-fulfilments/{ref}").

`copy` is the one operation that does not. `frontend:src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/create.js:31-46` makes a single call — `POST /notification-fulfilments/{sourceRef}/copy`. The backend handler `backend:.../notificationfulfilments/NotificationFulfilmentsService.java:106-113` mints its OWN new reference number for the copy and inserts only a `NotificationFulfilments` document. No `Notification` document is ever created at the copy's reference.

Three user-visible consequences follow, all confirmed by reading the code paths end to end:

1. **The copy never appears on "Your notifications".** `frontend:.../real/lifecycle/read.js:16-31` lists the dashboard from `GET /notifications` (the comment at :16-21 says so deliberately). The copy has no notification document, so it is absent from the list — permanently.
2. **Every page save on a copy fails with the service-error page.** `frontend:.../real/lifecycle/mutate.js:36-46` writes the notification projection with `POST /notifications` carrying `referenceNumber`. `backend:.../notification/NotificationService.java:86-92` routes a non-blank reference to `updateNotification`, which at `:381-384` throws `NotFoundException`. `frontend:.../real/projections/put-projection.js:17-38` retries three times then throws, and `.../real/projections/failure.js:4-19` converts that into the recoverable backend error — i.e. "Sorry, there is a problem with the service".
3. **A copy can never be submitted.** `finalise`/`amend`/`softDelete` all `POST /notifications/{ref}/...` (`transition.js:23-83`), which 404s for the copy's reference.

Note the frontend already *believes* `POST /notifications` is an upsert — `put-projection.js:6-8` states "Both projection variants — canonical PUT and main's POST /notifications — are idempotent whole-record writes on the backend". It is not: it 404s for an unknown reference. That mismatch is masked for journeys born through `create` (which mints the notification first) and is exposed only by copy.

This is new code: `git -C repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend log -- src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/create.js` returns only `23f2fdb4` (the EUDPA-288 model retrofit). The frontend unit test at `frontend:src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/real.requests.test.js:358-374` currently *pins* the single-sided write — every neighbouring test asserts a two-request dual write; the copy test asserts one. The shared port contract test (`records-port.test.js:209-236`) runs against the stub only (`records-port.test.js:2` imports `./stub/index.js`), and the stub's copy (`.../stub/lifecycle/create.js:22-51`) is a single in-memory store, so no unit test can see the split. The -tests E2E specs stop one assertion short: `tests:tests/e2e/pages/notification-dashboard.spec.ts:88-106` and `tests:tests/e2e/pages/notification-view-states.spec.ts:63-73` both click Copy as new, land on the hub, check the new reference differs — and stop, never returning to the dashboard and never saving a page on the copy.

Why this needs a ruling rather than a mechanical fix: there are two coherent repairs with different blast radius and a real trade-off between them.

(A) **Frontend-only, follows the documented `create` idiom.** Call `POST /notifications/{sourceRef}/copy` (already implemented — `backend:.../notification/NotificationController.java:55-66`, `NotificationService.java:95-106`) to mint the new reference and copy the notification content, then `GET /notification-fulfilments/{sourceRef}` and `PUT /notification-fulfilments/{newRef}` to bootstrap canonical (the PUT creates-if-absent — `NotificationFulfilmentsService.java:54-76`). Costs nothing in the backend, but abandons the fulfilments-side `Idempotency-Key` dedupe that was deliberately built (backend dedupe store, the hidden `idempotencyKey` form field in `dashboard/template.njk:94-96`, the per-row `randomUUID()` in `dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:22`, and the stub's `copiesBySourceAndKey` map). A double-click would then yield two drafts.

(B) **Keep the idempotent fulfilments copy as the reference minter, add the missing backend capability.** After the fulfilments copy returns the new reference, the frontend eagerly writes the notification projection for it via `fulfilmentToNotification`; this requires `POST /notifications` to create-at-supplied-reference when the reference is absent (i.e. make it the upsert `put-projection.js:6-8` already claims it is), which is a backend change plus a Java test. Preserves double-submit dedupe and makes the copy dashboard-visible immediately.

Both are defensible; picking one silently is how the idempotency machinery gets thrown away without anyone noticing. Hence the gate.
increments.refutation:
I tried to break this on all five fronts and could not. Every load-bearing claim reproduces in the code.

DEFECT EXISTS — CONFIRMED.
- `frontend:src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/create.js:31-46` — `copy` makes exactly one call, `POST ${notificationFulfilmentsUrl}/${journeyId}/copy`, and returns `marshal(await response.json())`. No notification-side write. Compare `create` at :11-29, which does both.
- `backend:.../notificationfulfilments/NotificationFulfilmentsService.java:106-115` — the copy mints its own ref via `referenceNumberGenerator.generate()` and `notificationFulfilmentsRepository.insert(copy)`. The class has only `NotificationFulfilmentsRepository` + `ReferenceNumberGenerator` injected (:24-32) — it cannot create a `Notification`. So after a copy, a `NotificationFulfilments` exists at the new ref and no `Notification` does.
- Real mode is what runs: `docker/stack/frontend.compose.yml:52` sets `LIVE_ANIMALS_MODE=real` (verified by grep).

CONSEQUENCES — CONFIRMED.
1. Dashboard: `frontend:.../real/lifecycle/read.js:22-48` lists from `GET ${notificationsUrl}?page=…`; backend `NotificationService.findAll` (:124-129) queries `notificationRepository`. No Notification doc ⇒ the copy is never listed.
2. Page save: `frontend:.../real/lifecycle/mutate.js:36-46` always includes the `POST /notifications` projection carrying `referenceNumber: journeyId`. `NotificationController.post` (:46-53) → `saveOriginOfImport` (:86-92) → non-blank ref → `updateNotification` (:381-384) → `NotFoundException`. `put-projection.js:9-38` exhausts retries and rethrows; `projections/failure.js:4-19` marks it recoverable.
3. Transitions: `transition.js:23-83` — finalise/amend/cancelAmend/softDelete all `POST ${notificationsUrl}/${journeyId}/…` in a `Promise.all`, each 404s for the copy's ref. The copy can never be submitted, and cannot even be deleted.

ROOT CAUSE, NOT SYMPTOM. I checked one level up (`engine/journey.js:136-144` `copyJourney` → `records.copy`, then `session.addKnownJourney`; `features/notification-actions/controller.js:25-41` redirects to `hubPath(copied.journeyId)`) and one level down (backend controller + repositories). Nothing else creates the missing aggregate. The single-sided call in `create.js:31-46` is the origin.

MATCHES THE SNAG. The specs prove copy currently *works up to the hub* (`tests:tests/e2e/pages/notification-dashboard.spec.ts:88-106` and `notification-view-states.spec.ts:63-73` both pass today: click, land on overview, new ref differs). So what a human would actually report as "Copy as new is broken" is exactly the residue — the copy vanishes from Your notifications and errors on every save. Match is good.

REPO LIST IS COMPLETE. frontend + tests are always needed; backend is needed under option B only (a superset is the right call at a gate). Nothing else is reachable — the stub repo, admin and reference-data have no part in this path.

VERDICT `needs-decision` HOLDS, and the trade-off is real, not invented. Option A's cost is not hypothetical: the idempotency machinery is deliberately built and indexed — `backend:.../NotificationFulfilments.java:43-45` declares a partial index `{'idempotencyKey': 1}` filtered on `{'idempotencyKey': {'$type':'string'}}`, `NotificationFulfilmentsController.java:110` makes the `Idempotency-Key` header *required*, and the service dedupes on it including the concurrent-insert path (`:90-95`, `:118-124`). There is no equivalent on `POST /notifications/{ref}/copy` (`NotificationController.java:55-66` → `copyNotification` :95-106 → plain `createNotification`). Option B changes the semantics of a public endpoint. The repo's own docs contradict each other on ordering — `frontend:src/server/app/docs/persistence.md:54-57` says canonical fulfilment first then projections, while `create.js:7-10` says notification mints the ref first — so there is no in-repo precedent that settles it. Gate is justified.

MISSED OPTION (add to the decision menu, does not break the diagnosis): (C) do the dual-create in the backend, inside the existing `@Transactional` on `NotificationFulfilmentsService.copy` (:84-131), so one call leaves both aggregates present. This is the only option that keeps the idempotency dedupe *and* leaves `POST /notifications` semantics untouched; its cost is coupling the two services, which is precisely the independence asserted at `:24-32`. Presenting only A and B understates the choice.

THREE PRECISION ERRORS IN THE WRITE-UP (none fatal, but they change what the implementor writes):
- "retries three times" — `real/config.js:9` sets `MAX_PROJECTION_ATTEMPTS = 2`, and `put-projection.js:17` loops to that.
- "fails with the service-error page" is wrong about the mechanism. `shared/kit.js:111-120` `recoverableSave` catches the recoverable error and each feature controller re-renders **the same page** at HTTP 500 with the `recoverableError` banner — see `features/origin/controller.js:132-142` and the copy text at `shared/copy.en.js:26-29` ("Sorry, there is a problem with the service. Your answers on this page have been saved."), rendered by `shared/layout.njk:58-61`. There is no navigation to an error page. The proposed E2E assertion "assert no service-error page" would therefore pass on the *unfixed* code — a toothless assertion. It must assert the banner text is absent and the response is not 500 / the journey advanced.
- "the copy test currently pins the single-sided write" overstates it: `real.requests.test.js:358-374` does `const [request] = fetchMocker.requests()` with no length assertion, so adding a second request would not turn it red. The correct framing is stronger for the investigator, not weaker — *nothing anywhere* catches this. `records-port.test.js:2` imports `./stub/index.js` only, confirming the contract test never sees the real adapter.

increments.notes: In real mode, Copy as new creates only the NotificationFulfilments aggregate at a freshly minted reference and never creates the matching Notification. I broke the diagnosis by rendering the page rather than reasoning about it. I signed into the running stack (localhost:3000 → Defra ID stub) at a 1440px viewport and read computed styles off the live dashboard.

WHAT THE INVESTIGATOR GOT WRONG. Their load-bearing claim is "THE CONTROL ITSELF IS NOT BROKEN ... the control did not regress ... the snag is a width regression, not a defect in the Copy-as-new control or in `.app-link-button`". That is false. Live computed styles on frontend `/live-animals`:
  - every `.app-link-button` ("Copy as new" x10, "Amend" x2) → `font-family: "Times"`, 19px, 700
  - every sibling `a.govuk-link` in the same `<ul>` ("View", "Resume", "Delete") → `font-family: "GDS Transport", arial, sans-serif`, 19px, 700
"Copy as new" is literally rendering in the browser default serif next to Arial/GDS Transport links. That is the snag, verbatim: "Copy as new CSS is off".

MECHANISM (root cause). frontend:src/client/stylesheets/core/_main.scss:16 `font-family: inherit`. In the compiled bundle `.public/stylesheets/application.1ee130c.min.css`: `.govuk-link,a{font-family:GDS Transport,arial,sans-serif;...}` at byte 941, `.app-link-button{...font-family:inherit;...}` at byte 137469. Equal specificity (0,1,0), later source order wins — so `inherit` beats the govuk font stack. Nothing up the chain supplies it: govuk-frontend 6.4.0 sets font-family only on component classes (I dumped all 52 `{font-family:GDS Transport…}` rules — none is `body`, `html`, `.govuk-template`, `.govuk-template__body`, `.govuk-width-container`, `.govuk-main-wrapper` or any grid class); `.govuk-summary-card__actions` (bundle 101825 + 101974) sets `font-size`/`font-weight` but no family; `.govuk-summary-card__title-wrapper` (101183) sets none. So the `<button>` inherits the document default. The `font-size: inherit` / `font-weight: inherit` lines are fine (19px/700 both) — only `font-family` is wrong.

WHY THE PROPOSED FIX DOES NOT FIX THE SNAG. Widening the column changes nothing about font-family. After the investigator's edit, "Copy as new" is still Times. An implementor would edit two working templates plus two test files, run a green ladder, and ship with the reported defect untouched.

SCOPE CHECK — the snag names "Copy as new" and only the dashboard instance is broken. On the check-answers/notification-view page (features/check-answers/template.njk:31-50) the same label renders as a `govukButton`, which sets its own font: I measured it at `/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-5GGXDG/notification-view` → `"GDS Transport", arial, sans-serif`, baseline-aligned with Delete at y=396. So that page is fine and `.app-form-inline{display:contents}` (bundle 137833) is working as intended. The defect is confined to `.app-link-button`.

THE WIDTH FINDING IS REAL BUT IS A DIFFERENT SNAG. I confirmed the arithmetic: `.govuk-grid-column-two-thirds` 660px → `.notification-list__layout` 630px → `.notification-list__filters` 280px (pinned at desktop, _notification-list.scss:112-115) → `.notification-list__main` 320px → `.govuk-summary-card__actions` 162px, and the four actions wrap onto three lines (View y=679 / Amend y=677, Copy as new y=713, Delete y=750). increments.title: Restrict allowed dates on the three MoJ date pickers (client + server)
increments.diagnosis:
Confirmed real, and it is not an EUDPA-288 regression — the restriction has never existed (`git -C repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend log --all -S minDate` returns nothing; `grep -rn "minDate|maxDate|excludedDates|excludedDays|weekStartDay"` over `src/` and `prototypes/` returns nothing).

There are exactly three MoJ date pickers in the live-animals journey, all rendered through one shared helper:
- `frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/exit-date/template.njk:13` → `mojDatePicker(exitDate)`, params built at `.../exit-date/controller.js:34-39`
- `frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/port-of-entry/port-of-entry.njk:16` → `mojDatePicker(arrivalDate)`, params built at `.../port-of-entry/port-of-entry.controller.js:86-91`
- `frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:41` → `mojDatePicker(dateOfIssue)`, params built at `.../documents/view-model/render.js:58-63`

Root cause, layer 1 (client): every one of those calls `kit.dateField` at `frontend:src/server/app/shared/kit.js:158-168`, which returns only `{ id, name, classes, label, hint, errorMessage, value }`. The MoJ 10.0.1 component reads its restrictions from `params.minDate`, `params.maxDate`, `params.excludedDates`, `params.excludedDays` and emits them as `data-min-date` / `data-max-date` / `data-excluded-dates` / `data-excluded-days` (`node_modules/@ministryofjustice/frontend/moj/components/date-picker/template.njk:10-36`). `dateField` has no parameter for any of them and no caller passes one, so every calendar renders fully open — any past or far-future date is selectable.

Root cause, layer 2 (server): the only date rule enforced on POST is calendar validity. `dateText` (`frontend:src/server/app/lib/validate/validators.js:190-203`) matches `^(\d{1,2})/(\d{1,2})/(\d{4})$` and calls `isRealDate` (`frontend:src/server/app/lib/validate/calendar.js:8-24`); there is no bounded-date validator in `validators.js` at all (the exported set is compose/requiredText/requiredExactDigits/optionalText/maxText/pattern/postcode/vehicleReg/ukPhone/requiredOneOf/oneOf/integerInRange/dateParts/dateText). All three controllers use it unbounded: `exit-date/controller.js:21`, `port-of-entry.controller.js:51`, `documents/form/payload.js:23`. So even once `data-min-date` lands, a JS-off user or a direct POST still saves an out-of-range date — the fix has to be both layers or it is cosmetic.

Why this is needs-decision and not actionable: nothing in the repo or the requirement source states what "restricted" means for these fields. The mined Confluence source of truth (`workareas/journey-builder/EUDPA-249/extract.confluence-v4.json:426-436` for `arrivalDateAtPort`, `:662-675` for `accompanyingDocumentDateOfIssue`) records `conditionsRaw: "Must be a valid date in DD/MM/YYYY format"` and nothing more; `exitDate` does not appear in the extract at all. The obligations carry no constraint either (`frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/arrival.js:5-9` is `{id, name, status: 'mandatory'}`). The three fields plainly want different rules — an expected exit date and an expected arrival at port are forward-looking, a document date of issue is backward-looking — and picking those bounds is a policy call, not a mechanical one. Guessing would also silently change validation of already-saved notifications.

Blast radius that makes this a two-repo fix: absolute dates are hard-coded either side of any future-only rule, and today is 2026-08-07 so some are already in the past. `frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/e2e/arrival-transit.e2e.spec.js:68` fills `03/01/2026`; `tests:flows/journey.ts:143` fills `12/12/2026`; `tests:tests/e2e/journeys/persistence/persistence-accompanying-document.spec.ts:29` pins `{day:'3',month:'1',year:'2026'}`. Any min-date rule turns those into fixtures that rot with the calendar, so they must move to dates computed relative to now as part of the same change.
increments.refutation:
I tried to break this on all five fronts and could not. Every load-bearing claim checks out against the code.

**1. Does the defect exist? Yes, verbatim.** Exactly three `mojDatePicker` call sites exist in `src/` (`frontend:.../transport/port-of-entry/port-of-entry.njk:16`, `.../documents/template.njk:41`, `.../exit-date/template.njk:13`) and zero in `prototypes/` (dir exists — `prototypes/standalone` — the grep genuinely returns nothing). `grep -rn "minDate|maxDate|excludedDates|excludedDays"` over the whole of `src/` returns nothing, and `git log --all -S minDate` returns nothing, so this is not an EUDPA-288 regression — it has never existed. Not `already-fixed`, not `cannot-reproduce`.

**2. Root cause, not symptom — and stronger than stated.** `frontend:src/server/app/shared/kit.js:158` is `dateField = (name, { label, hint, value = {}, error } = {})` returning only `{id, name, classes, label, hint, errorMessage, value}`. The MoJ 10.0.1 template reads `params.minDate`/`maxDate`/`excludedDates`/`excludedDays` (`node_modules/@ministryofjustice/frontend/moj/components/date-picker/template.njk:10-36`; README:29-33 documents them and pins the format as **dd/mm/yyyy**). `dateField` has no passthrough for them and no `attributes` escape hatch either, so all three render open. I also checked the layer the investigator did not: the client bundle IS wired (`src/client/javascripts/application.js:9,16` imports and `createAll(DatePicker)`), and the SCSS is imported (`application.scss:2`) — so there is no missing-bundle third cause. Reading `date-picker.mjs:301-317,513-519` actually *strengthens* the two-layer argument: `minDate`/`maxDate` only disable calendar cells and clamp the calendar's focus date — a user can still **type** an out-of-range date into the input with JS fully enabled. So server-side validation is not merely a no-JS fallback; without it the attributes are near-useless. Layer 2 confirmed: `validators.js:190-203` `dateText` does regex + `isValidCalendarDate` only, no bounded variant exists, and all three call sites use it unbounded (`exit-date/controller.js:21`, `port-of-entry.controller.js:51`, `documents/form/payload.js:23`).

**3. Does the diagnosis match the snag's words?** Mostly, with one caveat the ruling must dispose of. "MoJ date picker is used but doesn't have restricted dates" has a second defensible reading: the MoJ design system positions the date picker as the component *for* restricted date ranges, so the sentence can mean "we used the picker where there are no restrictions — wrong component, use `govukDateInput`". That reading inverts the entire changeset. I judge the investigator's reading the more natural one ("doesn't **have**" = lacks configuration), but this is further evidence for `needs-decision`, not against it, and the decision record should name and kill option B explicitly before an implementor starts.

**4. `needs-decision` is correct and I could not downgrade it.** There is genuinely no target in the repo. `workareas/journey-builder/EUDPA-249/extract.confluence-v4.json` gives only "Must be a valid date in DD/MM/YYYY format" for the two fields it covers, `exitDate` is absent entirely, and `.../obligations/sections/arrival.js:5-9` carries `{id, name, status}` and nothing else. The three fields want opposite-signed rules. This is a policy call.

**5. Repo list is correct — I considered and rejected `backend`.** `Transport.arrivalDate` (`backend:.../notification/Transport.java:17`) and `AccompanyingDocumentDto.dateOfIssue` are persisted, and `DocumentUploadRequest.java:25-27` carries `@NotNull` on `dateOfIssue` with no `@PastOrPresent`. `NotificationDto.java` has **no** jakarta.validation annotations at all. So the backend is not currently a date-validation surface for any of these fields; extending the bound to the API is a legitimate question for the ruling to answer, but it is hardening beyond this snag rather than a repo the fix *must* touch. Leaving it out of missingRepos deliberately.

**Where the investigator is genuinely incomplete (not wrong, but under-scoped): the fixture blast radius.** They listed 2 tests-repo files and 3 frontend spec lines. The real count is much larger, and a `needs-decision` writeup that under-states blast radius sends the implementor in short. Missed entirely: `tests:tests/a11y/notification-journey-filled-state.spec.ts:73`, `tests:tests/e2e/features/port-of-entry-select.spec.ts:20`, `tests:tests/e2e/features/documents-refresh-no-js.spec.ts:5`, `tests:tests/e2e/features/documents-reject.spec.ts:5`, `tests:tests/e2e/features/documents-limits.spec.ts:8`, `tests:tests/e2e/features/documents-scan-lifecycle.spec.ts:7`, `tests:tests/e2e/features/promoted-documents.spec.ts:12,41`, and `tests:tests/e2e/features/hub-groups-and-cya-rows.spec.ts:80` which *asserts* `toHaveText('12/12/2026')` and so breaks the moment `flows/journey.ts:143` is derelativised. On the frontend side they cited `arrival-transit.e2e.spec.js:68` but not its paired assertion at `:279`, and did not flag that `exit-date.e2e.spec.js:176,181` fills/asserts `27/3/2026` — already in the past as of 2026-08-07, so it dies under any future-only exit-date rule. increments.diagnosis:
The snag is about search UI that EXISTS and behaves badly, not about its absence. Two shipped surfaces are the likely referents, and the investigator missed both.

A. Notification dashboard search (`frontend:.../features/dashboard/template.njk:40-54`) — a Search box that only matches a complete reference number, case-sensitively. Stub: `frontend:src/server/app/services/persistence/records/stub/lifecycle/read.js:25` (`journey.id === referenceNumber`). Real: `backend:.../notification/NotificationService.java:130-140` via `NotificationRepository.findByReferenceNumberAndStatusIn` (`NotificationRepository.java:17`), documented as exact match at `NotificationController.java:139`. Typing part of a reference returns "No notifications found" — pinned at `tests:tests/e2e/features/notification-dashboard-search.spec.ts:45-60`. Fixing this reaches into the backend.

B. Address-book party picker (`frontend:.../features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:77-91`) — free-text `q` + a secondary Search submit + a radio table paginated at `PAGE_SIZE = 5` over ~40 records (`frontend:src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:26`), i.e. 8 pages. Every search and every page turn is a full page reload with selection smuggled through hidden fields and query strings (`party-picker.controller.js:94-97`, `view-model/pagination/results-href.js`). Shared by all five parties plus contact (`addresses/parties.js:15-63`). Pinned at `tests:page-objects/notification/party-picker-page.ts:21-26` and `tests:tests/e2e/features/addresses-picker.spec.ts`.

The investigator's "long selects have no type-ahead" finding is real and verified, but it is a separate concern that re-opens the deliberate EUDPA-288 ruling in `bc285d71` ("Enhanced search returns as a later round"). It should be the third item on the decision list, not the whole diagnosis. The gate question for Sam is: which surface — dashboard search matching, party-picker round-tripping, or long-select type-ahead — and only the third one is a reversal of a settled decision.
increments.refutation:
The diagnosis's load-bearing claim is factually wrong. It states "None of them has any filter, type-ahead or search affordance today" and builds the whole needs-decision gate on that absence. Two search affordances are shipped and live right now, and the investigator inventoried neither.

(1) NOTIFICATION DASHBOARD SEARCH — the first page a user sees. `frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/template.njk:40-54` renders a GET form with `govukInput` id/name `referenceNumber` and a `govukButton` labelled Search, inside an aside headed by `copy.search.heading`. It is exact-match-only on a complete reference: stub path `frontend:src/server/app/services/persistence/records/stub/lifecycle/read.js:25` filters `journey.id === referenceNumber`; real path `frontend:src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/read.js:27-28` forwards `&referenceNumber=` to the backend, where `backend:src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/animals/notification/NotificationService.java:130-140` calls `findByReferenceNumberAndStatusIn` (`backend:.../NotificationRepository.java:17`) — a single-document Optional, case-sensitive equality. The backend's own OpenAPI text admits it: `backend:.../NotificationController.java:139` "Optional referenceNumber: exact match against a complete notification reference." A partial reference returns nothing, pinned at `tests:tests/e2e/features/notification-dashboard-search.spec.ts:45-60` ("shows no notifications found when search text is free text"). A search box that only works if you paste the whole reference is a textbook "clunky af".

(2) ADDRESS-BOOK PARTY PICKER — `frontend:src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:77-91` is a text input `q` plus a secondary submit `name="action" value="search"` sharing one form with Save and continue; `:103-107` renders a paginated radio table. Every search and every page turn is a full server round-trip (`party-picker.controller.js:94-97` re-renders on `isSearchAction`), with selection carried in hidden fields and query strings (`view-model/pagination/results-href.js:3-13`). `frontend:src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:26` sets `PAGE_SIZE = 5` with a comment "40 records over 8 pages". This picker serves all five consignment parties plus contact (`.../addresses/parties.js:15-63`). It is pinned in the tests repo at `tests:page-objects/notification/party-picker-page.ts:21-26` (`get search`, `get searchButton`) and `tests:tests/e2e/features/addresses-picker.spec.ts`.

FRONT 3 — the diagnosis does not match the snag's words. "**The** autocomplete/search **stuff** is clunky af" is a definite-article, present-tense complaint about how existing things behave. The investigator's answer is "there is nothing there at all". Nobody looking at a bare `<select>` says "the search is clunky"; they say "there's no search". The two surfaces above are the overwhelmingly likelier referent, and the exact-match dashboard search in particular is clunky in exactly the way the word implies.

FRONT 1/2 — the investigator's secondary observations are accurate, and I verified them so as not to overcorrect: `port-of-entry.njk:18` is a bare `govukSelect` with `items: portItems`; `commodities/search/search.njk:19-29` is grouped `govukCheckboxes` with no input and no Search button; `grep` for `accessible-autocomplete|select-autocomplete|data-select-autocomplete` across `src/`, `package.json` and `webpack.config.js` returns nothing; commit `bc285d71` is exactly as described, message ending "Enhanced search returns as a later round." So the finding is real — but it is a *different* finding from the one the snag reports, and it re-litigates a settled EUDPA-288 ruling. Sending an implementor down that path first is precisely the churn the refute step exists to prevent.

FRONT 4 — repo list incomplete. If the referent is the dashboard search (the strongest candidate), the exact-match semantics live in the **backend**: any partial/contains/prefix match needs a new `NotificationRepository` query and a change to `NotificationService.findAll` (`NotificationService.java:124-148`), plus the real client and the OpenAPI description at `NotificationController.java:139`. `backend` is absent from the investigator's repo list. The root-cause file list also omits every party-picker and dashboard file.

FRONT 5 — the ladder is not honest for this snag. Steps 3-9 are frontend suites and step 11 is the tests repo; none of them touches either live search surface, so the ladder would pass byte-identically on unfixed code except for the specs the change itself edits. It also has no backend gate at all, and no pre-change baseline capture of the current search behaviour, so "less clunky" has nothing to be measured against.

VERDICT — `needs-decision` survives in kind (it is an aesthetic complaint with no target design in the repo or a cited Figma), but the diagnosis behind it does not. The decision to put to Sam is first "which of these surfaces did you mean", with the two shipped searches at the top, not "shall we reverse bc285d71".

FRONT 3 — the diagnosis does not match the snag. The reporter said "A11y tests failing from -tests repo". The investigator concluded a11y-specific page-object design debt. The evidence says every journey-entering spec fails, a11y and E2E alike, and no axe violation was found (all scans that ran were clean). Diagnosing an a11y problem here would send an implementor to write set-base plumbing that already exists.

FRONT 4 — repo list. The corrected verdict touches no repo, so `missingRepos` is empty. Worth flagging that the investigator's own list is internally inconsistent with the rest of the batch: every other EUDPA-315 snag (see tickets/snag-001-description.txt) is diagnosed against frontend main @23f2fdb4, so the batch's target is main, on which the page objects and the frontend already agree.

FRONT 5 — the ladder is dishonest by construction. Steps 1-3 (typecheck/lint/format:check) pass on the unfixed tree today. Step 4 runs `_assert_stack`, which does not currently know about journey bases, so it also passes unfixed. Steps 5-8 would go green simply by checking out `origin/spike/trace-to-requirements`, with zero new code — which is the tell that the ladder measures branch alignment, not a fix. Nothing in the ladder can fail in a way that distinguishes "I fixed the page objects" from "I fixed the environment".

Residual real item, separate from this snag and not what was reported: `test:docker-compose` (package.json:27) and `test:docker-compose:ci` (:29) both `--grep-invert '@a11y'`, and `_assert_stack` (:23) is defined but never invoked by any lane.
